raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible as an elevation-gradient single-column ensemble; ELM resolves the vertical water budget (P, ET, snow, infiltration, runoff generation) at each site, but true lateral hillslope/stream routing and glacier mass balance are out of single-column scope.",
    "answerable": [
      "Elevation-dependent partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, surface runoff, and subsurface drainage",
      "Snowpack accumulation/ablation (SWE, snow depth, melt timing) as a function of elevation",
      "Rain vs snow phase fractionation along the gradient",
      "Soil moisture storage and water-table depth response by elevation band",
      "Seasonal and interannual variability of the column water balance"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Integrated streamflow/discharge at the Bow River outlet (requires lateral routing model, e.g., MOSART)",
      "Lateral hillslope subsurface redistribution between columns",
      "Glacier ice dynamics and glacial meltwater contribution (not represented in standard ELM)",
      "Sub-grid avalanche/wind snow redistribution"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "Five columns span the ~1400–2900 m headwater relief of the Bow River in ~350 m increments, enough to resolve the montane-to-alpine transition in snow fraction, ET, and runoff while keeping the ensemble tractable for single-column ELM.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "BOW_1400_Banff", "lat": 51.18, "lon": -115.57, "soil_texture": "gravelly_sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "BOW_1540_LakeLouise", "lat": 51.43, "lon": -116.18, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "BOW_1920_BowLake", "lat": 51.67, "lon": -116.45, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "BOW_2350_BowSummit", "lat": 51.72, "lon": -116.50, "soil_texture": "stony_loam"},
    {"id": "BOW_2850_AlpineRidge", "lat": 51.60, "lon": -116.42, "soil_texture": "rocky_loamy_sand"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1995",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",
    "STOP_N": "20",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1995-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "RAIN", "SNOW", "QFLX_SNOW_GRND", "QFLX_RAIN_GRND",
      "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP", "FSNO", "QSNOMELT", "QSNOFRZ",
      "QINFL", "QOVER", "QRUNOFF", "QDRAI", "QRGWL",
      "QSOIL", "QVEGE", "QVEGT", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "FCEV", "FCTR", "FGEV",
      "H2OSOI", "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE", "ZWT", "WA", "TWS",
      "TSA", "TG", "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["elm_single_column"],
  "assumptions": [
    "Atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 by default) is topographically downscaled/lapse-rate corrected to each column elevation so that temperature and precipitation-phase gradients drive realistic snow partitioning; without downscaling all columns would share near-identical forcing.",
    "A 20-year spin-up (recycling 1995–2014) precedes the analysis run to equilibrate soil moisture, snow, and water-table states.",
    "Vegetation assigned from PFT distributions typical of the elevation band (montane needleleaf forest low, subalpine larch/spruce mid, alpine tundra/bare high).",
    "Each column is a vertical 1-D water balance; no inter-column lateral flow or river routing is included.",
    "Glaciated fractions near the highest sites are treated as seasonal snow only (no ice dynamics).",
    "Deep bedrock limits effective soil column depth at high-elevation rocky sites."
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as an elevation-gradient single-column ensemble; ELM resolves the vertical water budget (P, ET, snow, infiltration, runoff generation) at each site, but true lateral hillslope/stream routing and glacier mass balance are out of single-column scope.
answerable: Elevation-dependent partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, surface runoff, and subsurface drainage
Snowpack accumulation/ablation (SWE, snow depth, melt timing) as a function of elevation
Rain vs snow phase fractionation along the gradient
Soil moisture storage and water-table depth response by elevation band
Seasonal and interannual variability of the column water balance
not_answerable: Integrated streamflow/discharge at the Bow River outlet (requires lateral routing model, e.g., MOSART)
Lateral hillslope subsurface redistribution between columns
Glacier ice dynamics and glacial meltwater contribution (not represented in standard ELM)

parsed.n_justification: Five columns span the ~1400–2900 m headwater relief of the Bow River in ~350 m increments, enough to resolve the montane-to-alpine transition in snow fraction, ET, and runoff while keeping the ensemble tractable for single-column ELM.
assumptions: Atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 by default) is topographically downscaled/lapse-rate corrected to each column elevation so that temperature and precipitation-phase gradients drive realistic snow partitioning; without downscaling all columns would share near-identical forcing.
A 20-year spin-up (recycling 1995–2014) precedes the analysis run to equilibrate soil moisture, snow, and water-table states.
Vegetation assigned from PFT distributions typical of the elevation band (montane needleleaf forest low, subalpine larch/spruce mid, alpine tundra/bare high).
Each column is a vertical 1-D water balance; no inter-column lateral flow or river routing is included.
Glaciated fractions near the highest sites are treated as seasonal snow only (no ice dynamics).
Deep bedrock limits effective soil column depth at high-elevation rocky sites.
